span.label: priming as IMPLICIT - named by the paper as the critical feature of the theories it is testing, and stated as a double requirement: subjects identify primed material better AND cannot explicitly remember it. The effect is defined partly by a FAILURE that has to accompany it, which is why a study finding memory for the primes is testing something the definition cares about
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming defined by a PROPERTY LIST rather than by a mechanism - automatic, effortless, unconscious, neuroanatomically separate from sophisticated forms of memory such as episodic memory. Every item is a contrast with something else, and it is precisely this shape of definition that licenses the leap to evolutionary age: a capacity that needs none of the expensive machinery is assumed to have come first
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the PHYLOGENETIC ASSUMPTION, named as an assumption in the abstract: priming is `commonly thought, WITH LITTLE EVIDENCE, to be widely distributed phylogenetically`. The paper's target is not a finding but a belief its field holds without having tested it - and the only prior nonhuman evidence it can find is one study in pigeons
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: search image versus perceptual priming - a neighbouring concept separated by two stated measurements rather than by definition: the search image is SHORT LIVED and is DIMINISHED BY DIVIDED ATTENTION, so it is classed as short-term ATTENTIONAL priming rather than the long-term PERCEPTUAL priming seen in humans. Two literatures using one word, told apart by duration and by whether attention matters
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `priming` and `perceptual priming` are used at DIFFERENT GRAIN in different parts of the argument, and the split is systematic rather than casual: where the paper reasons about memory SYSTEMS - dissociation from explicit memory, survival in amnesia, evolutionary age - it writes bare `priming`; where it describes the visual effect it measures, and where it fences that effect off from the search image, it writes `perceptual priming`. The general term carries the theory and the specific term carries the experiment
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a null defended rather than reported - the paper argues its own absence of evidence is not absence of power, on three separate grounds: priming is routinely seen in SINGLE human subjects, the pigeon result that motivated the study used FEWER subjects than this one, and the same animals demonstrably remembered the primes. The last is the one that matters, because it rules out the animals not having encoded the images at all
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: perceptual priming —distinct-from→ search image
span.note: differs in: DURATION AND ATTENTIONAL DEPENDENCE - the search image is short lived and is diminished by divided attention, which is why the paper files it as short-term attentional priming rather than long-term perceptual priming · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The paper's own phrase is `similar to, but distinct from`, and it does not leave the distinction as an assertion: both differentiating properties are cited to experiments. This is the shape the corpus wants - a boundary drawn with measurements.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming —distinct-from→ explicit memory
span.note: differs in: WHETHER IT SURVIVES AMNESIA AND WHICH NEURAL SYSTEM CARRIES IT - the separation is the definition rather than a finding about it, which is what makes this record's null result awkward for the theory · strength of the relation: 0.9 — Recorded because the dissociation is doing definitional work: priming is IDENTIFIED by being separable from explicit memory. A monkey that recognises the primes but shows no priming is a dissociation running the other way.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: repetition suppression —causes→ priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.7 — Weight 0.7 - the LOWEST on this record, and deliberately. The paper reports this as a theorised mechanism it is about to find fault with: the neural signature is present in monkeys and the behavioural effect is not. Recorded as the literature's claim, not as this paper's.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: recognition —distinct-from→ classification
span.note: differs in: WHETHER MEMORY FOR AN IMAGE REACHES THE PROCESS AT ALL - the same remembered image supports recognition and does nothing for classification, which the paper reads as cognitive encapsulation between the two · strength of the relation: 0.85 — THE RESULT, stated as a relation between two tasks rather than as an effect size. The paper's last word on it is `presents a puzzle`, and the weight says so.

span.label: Across eleven experiments rhesus monkeys showed no priming: previously seen images conferred no reliable advantage when degraded versions had to be classified.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same monkeys did recognise the prime images, both masked and unmasked, at the same memory interval at which no priming appeared.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The single significant priming result (the blur-mask experiment) failed to replicate under stronger conditions and is interpreted as a Type I error.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Shuffling the visible fragments of a masked image lowered classification accuracy, showing the monkeys used global arrangement rather than isolated local features.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The classification was based on global form, exactly the kind of process that memory for the intact image should have facilitated.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A close methodological replication of the only positive nonhuman priming study (in pigeons) produced no priming in monkeys.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The combination of intact recognition with absent facilitation constitutes a dissociation between remembering an image and classifying it.
